Visual and Media Arts Grants, Fellowships and Residencies

Currently 249 active paid visual and media arts grants, fellowships and residencies. Hand-curated and updated weekly. Almost every entry is funded; a few notable unpaid open calls and festival submissions are included as clearly flagged exceptions. Browse the list below, or use the interactive desk for filtering and shortlisting.

Subscribe: RSS feed · Calendar (.ics)

Open calls

  1. dm-Award connecting worlds 2027: PLAYGROUND (projection mapping and public-space media art, EUR 10,000 prize plus up to EUR 20,000 production, SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE Karlsruhe)

    Karlsruhe UNESCO City of Media Arts Office (Cultural Office), with dm-drogerie markt, ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe and KME Karlsruhe Marketing und Event · Karlsruhe, Germany (palace facade and Market Square). Open internationally to individual artists and collectives. · Deadline: 25 Nov 2026 · Award: EUR 10,000 prize plus up to EUR 20,000 net production funding for the winning project (covering fees, technical equipment and travel), with curatorial and technical support from the Cultural Office, KME and ZKM.

    The UNESCO City of Media Arts Office of Karlsruhe's Department of Cultural Affairs awards the dm-Award connecting worlds, with dm-drogerie markt as awarding partner, ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe as curatorial partner and KME as organiser of the SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE Light Festival. Under the motto PLAYGROUND, the call seeks projects that connect the digital space of the projection mappings on Karlsruhe Palace's facade with the analogue space of the Market Square, playfully activating public space. FORMAT: every project must have two elements: a projection mapping on the palace facade (2 to 5 minutes) and at least one satellite on the Market Square that also works independently of the projection and is publicly and freely accessible. Examples include interactive projections and game elements with audience participation, installations or media artworks relating to the projection, combinations of performance, concerts or actions with projection mapping, sculptural, 3D or immersive formats, new technologies, and collaborations between local and international players. The winner is realised in 2027 during the SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE and the exhibition Media art is here, running four weeks between mid-August and mid-September 2027. WHO: artists worldwide, individually or as a collective. WHAT YOU GET: a EUR 10,000 prize, up to EUR 20,000 net production funding (which must cover all production costs, including fees, equipment and the winners' travel), plus curatorial and technical support; technical requirements are set out in the Production Guidelines. APPLICATION: via the call page; questions to cityofmediaarts@kultur.karlsruhe.de. Application period 9 October to 25 November 2026, closing at 13:00 CET.

  2. BBBank Award in Projection Mapping 2027: PLAYGROUND (ZKM, SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE Karlsruhe)

    ZKM | Center for Art and Media Karlsruhe, with BBBank and SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE Karlsruhe · Karlsruhe, Germany (palace facade). Open internationally. · Deadline: 25 Nov 2026 · Award: EUR 10,000 prize if the selected concept is realised, plus EUR 10,000 production funding covering fees and technology. No application fee.

    Open call for a 7-minute projection mapping on the Karlsruhe palace facade, on the 2027 festival theme Playground (The Art of Playing). For artists, designers, studios and collectives working in projection mapping; ZKM provides curatorial and technical coaching. APPLICATION (German or English, via the ZKM web form https://webform.zkm.de/form/bbbank-award-2027): concept or storyboard description (max 2,000 characters), a 5-second media check file following the technical guidelines, a short bio (max 1,000 characters) and a portrait photo. CONDITIONS: concepts must not have won other prizes or been submitted to comparable competitions (this is a separate call from the dm-Award connecting worlds at the same festival); finalists perform the work exclusively at SCHLOSSLICHTSPIELE; winners must attend the award ceremony. Deadline 25 November 2026, 1 pm CET.

  3. Canada Council: Creating, Knowing and Sharing, Short-Term Projects (First Nations, Inuit and Metis arts, Nov 2026 round)

    Canada Council for the Arts · Canada. For First Nations, Inuit and Metis artists, groups and organizations. · Deadline: 25 Nov 2026 · Award: Project grant; amounts set in the program guidelines on the Council's portal. No application fee stated.

    Creating, Knowing and Sharing is the Canada Council's program for the arts and cultures of First Nations, Inuit and Metis peoples. The Short-Term Projects component funds individual First Nations, Inuit and Metis artists, groups and organizations for projects including creation, production, knowledge transfer and sharing of work, in any artistic practice including media and digital arts. DEADLINE: 25 November 2026 (notification usually within 4 months). The related Small-Scale Activities and Travel components accept applications on a rolling basis before the activity starts. Apply through the Canada Council portal; Application Assistance is available for applicants who self-identify as First Nations, Inuit or Metis, or as Deaf or disabled.

  4. BC Arts Council Individual Arts Grants: Visual Artists, Crafts Artists, Critics and Curators (Nov 2026 intake)

    BC Arts Council (Province of British Columbia) · British Columbia. BC residents for at least 12 months, Canadian citizens or permanent residents. · Deadline: 25 Nov 2026 · Award: Up to CAD 15,000, up to 100% of eligible project expenses. No application fee.

    This BC Arts Council program supports established professional visual artists, contemporary and traditional craft artists, and independent visual and media arts critics and curators with the creation of specific new projects; projects may investigate visual arts, media arts and/or museum practice. Collaborations of two or more artists sharing creative control can apply through a single eligible lead applicant. AMOUNT: up to CAD 15,000, covering up to 100% of eligible project expenses; the council typically funds 20 to 30% of eligible applications. ELIGIBILITY: Canadian citizen or permanent resident; BC resident for at least 12 continuous months before the closing date; established practice with exhibitions or professional activity paid at CARFAC rates or equivalent. Media artists whose projects are media-arts focused are not eligible here (they apply to the separate Media Artists program, which closed in June 2026 and reopens in spring 2027). REGISTRATION: new applicants must register a profile by 18 November 2026. DEADLINE: 25 November 2026, 11:59 pm Pacific, via the BC Arts Council grant management system.

  5. Ljudmila: Parameter Generative Arts Fair at Adela Festival 2027 (open call)

    Ljudmila Art and Science Laboratory · Kino Siska, Ljubljana, Slovenia (fair on Saturday 6 March 2027, part of the Adela Festival 2027). Artists present in person. · Deadline: 26 Nov 2026 · Award: NO artist fee or production budget for the fair itself. Accommodation provided and travel reimbursed up to EUR 150. Jury prize: a solo exhibition at Kino Siska in 2028 with a EUR 700 gross artist fee. Two honorary mentions of EUR 350 gross each. Artists may sell work at the fair with no commission taken. No application or participation fees.

    Ljudmila Art and Science Laboratory invites artists to present and sell existing works at Parameter, a generative arts fair held during the Adela Festival 2027 at Kino Siska in Ljubljana. The call seeks work connected to a broader community engaging art, open-source technologies, creative coding, media archaeology, permacomputing and experimental electronics, broadening current concepts and implementations of generativity. SELECTION: up to 11 artists, who present their works at the fair on Saturday 6 March 2027 and are included in the print and web catalogue. SUPPORT: accommodation provided, travel costs reimbursed up to EUR 150; apply with existing works, as there is no production budget or artist fee. No application fees, no participation fees and no commission on sold works. AWARDS: the jury awards one prize, a solo exhibition at Kino Siska in 2028 with a EUR 700 gross artist fee, plus two honorary mentions of EUR 350 gross each. APPLICATION: via the online application form; the full open call is on the Ljudmila website. DEADLINE: Thursday 26 November 2026.

  6. Toronto Arts Council Open Door 2027 (strategic grant for Toronto arts organizations and collectives)

    Toronto Arts Council (TAC) · City of Toronto. Applicants must be located in Toronto. · Deadline: 26 Nov 2026 · Award: Project grant; amounts set in the 2027 Open Door guidelines. Accessibility add-on up to CAD 5,000 for Deaf artists and artists with disabilities. No application fee.

    Open Door is Toronto Arts Council's strategic grant for new or significantly expanded initiatives by Toronto arts organizations and artist collectives, open to any discipline including media and digital arts. ELIGIBILITY: located in the City of Toronto; incorporated non-profit arts organization or an artist collective operating on a not-for-profit basis (individuals are not funded); a viable administrative and financial plan; one Open Door grant per applicant every two years. Applicants are encouraged to contact the program manager before applying. TIMING: activities may not start until 3 months after the deadline, and projects must finish within two years of the notification letter. DEADLINE: 26 November 2026, 11:59 pm, via TAC Grants Online.

  7. Arts Council of Northern Ireland: Individual Artists Digital Evolution Awards 2026/27 (up to GBP 10,000 for digital art)

    Arts Council of Northern Ireland (National Lottery funded) · Northern Ireland. Applicants must live in Northern Ireland. · Deadline: 26 Nov 2026 · Award: Up to GBP 10,000 per award. The applicant's own artist fees can be budgeted at up to GBP 125 a day or GBP 500 a week. No application fee stated.

    A National Lottery award from the Arts Council of Northern Ireland for individual artists to make digital art and build skills in new media and immersive practice. WHAT COUNTS: art created exclusively in the digital space, or translated into physical form through technology, including AR and VR, 3D and digital creation, data-driven work and app-based art. Simple digitisation of existing work and filmed performances or recordings are excluded. WHO: individual artists of any discipline who live in Northern Ireland, are 18 or over, and have made a significant contribution to the arts there for at least one year in the last five. Partnership projects are possible with the artist as lead. University staff and students can apply only if the project is not part of their job or studies. Not eligible: artists who have had two of these awards in the past five years, and social media content creators. AMOUNT: up to GBP 10,000, for projects running between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028. Decisions are expected in February 2027. HOW TO APPLY: online only through the Arts Council's grants portal, linked from the programme page, with the budget template and all mandatory enclosures. DEADLINE: Thursday 26 November 2026 at 12 noon; the system shuts at noon precisely and uploads must be complete by then.

  8. Theatertreffen International Forum 2027, Berlin: 18-day scholarship for emerging theatre makers (all costs covered, no stipend)

    Berliner Festspiele, Theatertreffen, with the Goethe-Institut, Pro Helvetia and partners · Uferstudios and Theatertreffen venues, Berlin, Germany. Open to theatre makers from all parts of the world. · Deadline: 26 Nov 2026 · Award: NO CASH STIPEND; listed as a deliberate exception. The scholarship covers all participation costs: festival tickets, travel, Berlin public transport, shared accommodation, catering or a per diem, travel and health insurance and visa fees for those not resident in Berlin. No application fee mentioned.

    Around 30 theatre makers at the start of their practice spend the whole of Theatertreffen 2027 in Berlin together: watching the invited productions, taking workshops with artists, joining artist talks and excursions, and meeting the festival director and jury. The 2027 theme is The Art of Watching Theatre. WHO: practitioners from any performing-arts discipline, working across disciplines welcome, with around five years of professional experience and aged roughly 25 to 35; the stage reached in your development matters more than exact age. Good English is required. Only one named person per collective may apply, and you must be free for the whole forum and the online meetings. No nationality limit. WHAT YOU GET: no fee or stipend, but every cost of taking part is covered, including travel, a shared apartment, a per diem or catering, insurance and visa fees. APPLICATION: if your main place of work is Germany, Austria, Luxembourg or Switzerland, apply by email to Berliner Festspiele; everyone else applies through the Goethe-Institut portal. Send the application form, a photo answering the question What does theatre look like for you today?, a motivation letter of up to two pages on three set questions, a one-page artistic CV, and work samples of up to 10 pages and 5 MB. DEADLINE: 26 November 2026, 23:59 CET. Fellows are announced in late February 2027.

  9. Casa de Velazquez: Artists in Residence 2027-2028 (Academie de France a Madrid)

    Casa de Velazquez, Academie de France a Madrid · Madrid, Spain (residence at the Casa de Velazquez). No nationality requirement, but EU/Schengen nationals must be affiliated to an artist/author or self-employed scheme in their country of residence, and non-EU applicants need a French residence permit allowing work or a Schengen work and residence permit from another EU state. Good French required. · Deadline: 27 Nov 2026 · Award: Monthly residency grant voted each year; for 2026-2027 it was EUR 3,600 per month for artists housed at the Casa and EUR 4,600 per month for artists living outside (with children). Twelve monthly payments, September 2027 to August 2028. Housing and studio provided; a production support fund is also available on project. No application fee.

    The Academie de France a Madrid at the Casa de Velazquez offers 12 one-year residencies for 2027-2028 to young graduates and established artists developing a creative project in the Iberian Peninsula. Applicants declare one main discipline: drawing, printmaking, sculpture, painting, architecture, music composition, choreography, photography, or film and video (multidisciplinary development during the year is welcome). REQUIREMENTS: over 18; a higher arts diploma or a body of work judged by the committee; good French (application and interview in French); individual applications only (no collectives); at most three applications per lifetime. STATUS: EU/Schengen nationals must show affiliation to an artist/author or self-employed scheme; non-EU applicants need a French residence permit allowing work (to join URSSAF artists/authors) or a Schengen residence and work permit from another EU state plus artist-author status there, covering the whole residency. APPLICATION: online portal with a project of up to 5,000 characters in French, expectations and career fit (600 characters each), CV in French (max 3 pages), portfolio (A3 landscape PDF, max 10 pages), up to two video links of max 10 minutes, audio files (composers must include a chamber or orchestral work with score), up to 10 photos and up to two recommendation letters. SELECTION: pre-selection the week of 8 March 2027, interviews in French in Paris the week of 5 April 2027, results mid-April 2027. Residents must live at the Casa outside closure periods and take part in its exhibitions and concerts. DEADLINE: 27 November 2026, 13:00 Madrid time. Questions: candidatures-cvz@casadevelazquez.org.

The fellow spends one month in Venice: half the time as an exhibition ambassador at the British Pavilion (stewarding, engaging visitors, supporting daily gallery operations) and half on independent research or a creative or architectural project inspired by Venice, the Pavilion and the Biennale themes. Fellows complete 15 hours of online training in March-April 2027 and, on return, run a sharing session, workshop or exhibition for DOMA Initiatives. HOW TO APPLY: complete the application form (Google Doc linked from the call page) and email it with a CV and portfolio/research proposal to the selection committee. Shortlisting and interviews 30 November to 3 December 2026; nomination to the British Council 4 December 2026; final selection announced January 2027. Contact: Veronica Ng, DOMA Initiatives Coordinator, veronican@sunway.edu.my. DEADLINE: 27 November 2026, 12:00 noon MYT.

  12. University of Exeter Arts and Culture: Arts Commission 2026/27 (organisational cultures and narrative infrastructure)

    University of Exeter Arts and Culture, with the Faculty of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences (HASS) · Exeter, UK (Streatham campus, with some activity possible at Penryn, Cornwall). Minimum two days a month in person and online, January to June 2027. No nationality or residence restriction stated. · Deadline: 29 Nov 2026 · Award: Artist fee GBP 14,000 (incl. VAT, also covering travel, subsistence and accommodation) plus a production and presentation budget of up to GBP 4,000; a freelance creative producer is paid separately. Interviewed candidates receive GBP 100. No application fee.

    The University of Exeter's annual flagship Arts Commission invites a creative practitioner in any artform interested in organisational cultures (how people work together in formal settings, and how those cultures can be disrupted, adjusted and reimagined) to work with academics in the Faculty of Humanities, Arts and Social Sciences. Lines of enquiry: the role of narrative infrastructure across departments, networks and systems; how Humanities expertise shapes interdisciplinary research cultures; how these practices collide with entrenched institutional norms; and how they serve challenge-led priorities in the sector. The artist spends at least two days a month with HASS staff from January to June 2027 (conversations, team meetings, site visits, teaching, workshops with staff, students and publics), supported by an academic working group and a freelance creative producer, and creates a new artwork (performance, exhibition, reading, screening or other format) presented by the end of July 2027. The artist keeps ownership of the work; the process is documented in a short film. PAY: GBP 14,000 fee (incl. VAT, also covering travel, subsistence and accommodation) plus up to GBP 4,000 for production and presentation. CRITERIA: at least five years' professional practice with recognised work; experience of creative collaborations with academics or in higher education; a track record of facilitating varied stakeholders; previous work on organisational cultures, research cultures, narrative infrastructure or interdisciplinarity; strong budget and time management. TO APPLY: email a 1 to 2 page statement, CV and 3 to 4 work examples to artsandculture@exeter.ac.uk with subject 'Arts Commission 2026'. Online interviews 10 and 14 December 2026 (interviewees paid GBP 100). DEADLINE: 29 November 2026, 17:00 UK time.

Cultural institutions, vocational education institutions and interdisciplinary makers. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: EUR 5,000 to EUR 75,000 depending on the scheme (e.g. cultural education in mbo EUR 5,000-55,000, in vmbo/vso/pro EUR 10,000-65,000, design-based learning platforms up to EUR 75,000, interdisciplinary makers EUR 12,500-50,000). No application fee.

    The Fonds voor Cultuurparticipatie, one of the Dutch national cultural funds (annual budget around EUR 30 million), currently has several schemes open for applications: cultural education in vocational education (mbo, EUR 5,000-55,000), cultural education in vmbo/vso/pro (EUR 10,000-65,000), cultural education for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom (EUR 5,000-50,000), an open call for design-based learning platforms (up to EUR 75,000) and an interdisciplinary scheme for professional makers (EUR 12,500-50,000). Most schemes target cultural institutions, in some cases in partnership with schools. See the subsidies overview for per-scheme conditions. No application fee.

  225. Arts Council England: National Lottery Project Grants (rolling)

    Arts Council England · England, UK. For individual practitioners and organisations; funded activity must primarily benefit audiences in England. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: GBP 1,000 to GBP 100,000 per project. Decisions in about 8 weeks for requests up to GBP 30,000, about 12 weeks above that. No application fee.

    England's main always-open public funding route for project work: individual artists, freelancers, collectives and cultural organisations can apply at any time for GBP 1,000 to 100,000. Supported disciplines span visual arts, combined arts (including festivals), dance, theatre, music, literature, museums and libraries, and the fund regularly backs digital and interdisciplinary work within those. WHAT YOU GET: project funding covering artist fees, production, R&D within a project, touring or presentation, with decisions in roughly 8 weeks under GBP 30,000 and 12 weeks above. ELIGIBILITY: applicants based in England (others can apply if the activity substantially takes place in England and benefits English audiences); individuals must be 18+. DEADLINE: none, rolling applications via Grantium on artscouncil.org.uk.

  226. Creative Scotland: Open Fund for Individuals (rolling)

    Creative Scotland · Scotland, UK. For artists and creative practitioners based in Scotland. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: GBP 500 to GBP 50,000 (two levels: up to GBP 20,000 with decisions in 10 weeks, GBP 20,001 to 50,000 in 14 weeks). National Lottery funded. No application fee.

    Scotland's main always-open fund for individual artists and freelance creative practitioners across all artforms, including visual art, moving image, sound, digital and cross-disciplinary practice. It supports the development of creative practice and new work: research, experimentation, creation, collaboration, professional development and small-scale presentation. WHAT YOU GET: GBP 500 to 50,000 covering artist time at fair pay rates, materials, access costs and project costs; decisions in 10 weeks for requests up to GBP 20,000 and 14 weeks up to GBP 50,000. ELIGIBILITY: individuals based in Scotland (not organisations; a separate Open Fund serves them). DEADLINE: none, rolling applications via the Creative Scotland portal, subject to available budget.

  227. Fonds Podiumkunsten: Internationale Werkreis voor Individuen (international work trips for performing artists, rolling)

    Fonds Podiumkunsten (Performing Arts Fund NL) · Netherlands. For individual professional performing artists active in Dutch performing arts practice; trips take place abroad. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Up to EUR 2,500 for trips within Europe or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, up to EUR 4,000 for trips elsewhere, covering travel and accommodation. 2026 budget EUR 200,000, handled first come first served. No application fee.

    The Performing Arts Fund NL's Internationale Werkreis voor Individuen pays travel and accommodation for a short trip abroad that serves your artistic orientation or professional development: conferences, workshops, lectures, panels and festivals without a sales or performance goal. Makers may also attend an invited performance of existing work abroad if they add an activity such as a rehearsal, lecture or workshop. WHO: individual professional performing artists (theatre, dance, music, music theatre, performance) active in the Dutch performing arts field. WHAT YOU GET: up to EUR 2,500 (Europe and Caribbean Netherlands) or EUR 4,000 (rest of the world) per trip; one award per calendar year. APPLICATION: rolling via Mijn Fonds from 16 weeks to 4 weeks before the first activity, while the annual budget lasts. DEADLINE: rolling.

  228. Fonds Podiumkunsten: Snelloket for Dutch performances or concerts abroad (rolling)

    Fonds Podiumkunsten (Performing Arts Fund NL) · Netherlands. For Dutch groups and performers organised as a legal entity (stichting, vereniging, bv or nv), or their management, booking agency or label, performing abroad. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Up to EUR 10,000 per application: up to EUR 6,000 for performances within Europe, up to EUR 10,000 outside Europe (Caribbean inter-island travel up to EUR 6,000). Covers travel, transport and visa costs only. 2026 budget EUR 1,300,000. No application fee.

    The Snelloket is the Performing Arts Fund NL's fast-track touring grant for Dutch companies, ensembles, bands, performance makers and DJs invited to perform abroad. WHO: groups or performers with legal personality (stichting, vereniging, bv or nv; sole traders and partnerships are excluded) that have given at least ten professional performances at relevant Dutch venues or festivals in the previous 18 months. A management, booking agency or label with a structural relationship may apply on the artist's behalf. WHAT IT FUNDS: travel, transport and visa costs for at least three consecutive performances confirmed by foreign venues or festivals; flights under 600 km, accommodation and per diems are excluded. WHAT YOU GET: up to EUR 6,000 within Europe or EUR 10,000 outside Europe per application, twice a year at most. APPLICATION: rolling via Mijn Fonds, between four months and one month before the first show, with a decision within a month. DEADLINE: rolling.

  229. Mondriaan Fund: International Art Presentation (rolling, for foreign institutions and festivals presenting Dutch artists)

    Mondriaan Fund (Mondriaan Fonds) · For internationally recognised non-commercial art institutions and festivals outside the Netherlands presenting living visual artists from the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom; Dutch artists can also apply for their own costs. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Contribution towards extra costs: return travel for artists and guest curators, up to EUR 1,000 per person for lodging, transport and insurance of the work, up to 50 percent of production costs for new site-specific work, up to 25 percent of publication costs and up to 50 percent of film subtitling. No overall cap stated. No application fee.

    The Mondriaan Fund's International Art Presentation grant helps art institutions and festivals abroad present current work by living visual artists from the Netherlands or the Caribbean part of the Kingdom, covering costs that raise the work's visibility and fall outside the host's regular budget. WHO: internationally recognised institutions outside the Kingdom whose main purpose is showing contemporary art (not sales); commercial galleries are excluded (they use Art Fair International). Dutch and Caribbean-Kingdom artists with at least one year of professional practice can apply for their own personal costs. WHAT IS FUNDED: return travel for the artist and guest curator (one production trip and one opening visit), up to EUR 1,000 per person for lodging, transport and insurance of the work, up to 50 percent of production costs for new site-specific commissions (the host must pay the artist a realistic fee), up to 25 percent of publication costs and up to 50 percent of film subtitling. Artists may not be asked to pay to take part. Guest curators from the Netherlands need at least two years of curatorial experience. APPLICATION: via the Mondriaan Fund's My Fund system with a plan, presentation plan, CVs, consent declaration, itemised budget excluding VAT, quotes above EUR 1,000 and visual documentation; processing takes about three months. DEADLINE: rolling.

  230. Pro Helvetia: Visual Arts Event outside Switzerland (rolling up to CHF 50,000, for institutions and festivals presenting Swiss artists)

    Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council) · For established cultural institutions and festivals with international reach outside Switzerland presenting contemporary artists, photographers or architects from Switzerland. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Requests in three tiers: up to CHF 25,000 and CHF 25,001-50,000 (both year-round), and over CHF 50,000 (fixed deadlines). Covers transport and insurance, equipment rental, materials for temporary works, artist, photographer and architect fees, and economy travel for the Swiss participants. No application fee.

    Pro Helvetia supports presentations outside Switzerland of contemporary artists, photographers and architects from Switzerland, with applications generally made by the host institution or festival. WHO: established cultural institutions and organisers with international reach based outside Switzerland; exhibitions normally run at least four weeks, which does not apply to festivals and similar events. WHAT IS FUNDED: transport and insurance, equipment rental, materials for temporary artworks, fees for the participating artists, photographers and architects from Switzerland, and their economy-class travel (no accommodation). TIMELINE: requests up to CHF 25,000 can be submitted year-round with a decision within eight weeks; CHF 25,001 to 50,000 year-round with a decision within four months; over CHF 50,000 by 1 March, 1 June, 1 September or 1 December. Projects need a clear connection to Switzerland, and only complete, on-time applications are considered. APPLICATION: via the Pro Helvetia online portal. DEADLINE: rolling (fixed dates for requests over CHF 50,000).

  231. Pro Helvetia: Design Exhibition and Knowledge Exchange abroad (rolling, up to CHF 10,000 for design festivals and design weeks)

    Pro Helvetia (Swiss Arts Council) · For recognised design institutions and established design festivals or design weeks outside Switzerland featuring designers from Switzerland. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Up to CHF 10,000 towards transport and insurance and economy return travel (no accommodation). No application fee.

    Pro Helvetia funds thematic group exhibitions of design from Switzerland and knowledge exchange at public specialist events abroad, such as symposia and round tables, organised by institutions outside Switzerland. WHO: recognised design institutions and established festivals or design weeks outside Switzerland. WHAT YOU GET: up to CHF 10,000 for transport and insurance costs and economy-class return travel for participants from Switzerland (accommodation not covered). APPLICATION: year-round via the Pro Helvetia online portal; the project can start eight weeks after submission and decisions come within eight weeks. DEADLINE: rolling.

  232. Wales Arts International: International Opportunities Fund (rolling, up to GBP 7,500 for presenting work and collaborating abroad)

    Wales Arts International (Arts Council of Wales) · For arts organisations, individual creative professionals and collectives based in Wales; activity takes place in person outside Wales and the UK with at least one international partner. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Up to GBP 7,500 for international collaboration, presentation of work, and networks and events; up to GBP 5,000 for international residencies (up to GBP 7,500 outside Europe with prior approval). Covers up to 90 percent of eligible costs. No application fee.

    Wales Arts International's International Opportunities Fund supports Wales-based creative professionals and arts organisations to build relationships, collaborations and networks abroad, share skills internationally and raise Wales's profile. WHO: arts organisations, individual creative professionals and formal or informal collectives based in Wales (unconstituted groups need one lead applicant). WHAT IS FUNDED: in-person, arts-focused activity outside Wales and the UK with at least one international partner, such as presenting work at an international partner's invitation (where the partner pays at least an appropriate fee), attending international networks and events, collaboration and partnership development, and residencies organised by an international partner. WHAT YOU GET: up to GBP 7,500 for collaboration, presentation, and networks and events, or up to GBP 5,000 for residencies (GBP 7,500 outside Europe with prior approval), covering up to 90 percent of eligible costs. Artists, bands, songwriters or producers invited to international showcase festivals should use the PRS Foundation International Showcase Fund instead. APPLICATION: rolling via the Arts Council of Wales portal; projects must start at least 10 working weeks after submission. DEADLINE: rolling.

  233. Creative Debuts: Black Artists Grant (BAG), GBP 500 monthly no-strings grant for UK-based Black artists (rolling)

    Creative Debuts · UK (remote application). Applicants must be based in the UK. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: GBP 500 per recipient, one recipient per month. Unrestricted, no outcomes or reporting required. No application fee.

    The Black Artists Grant (BAG) is a no-strings-attached monthly grant run and sponsored by Creative Debuts, the London-based platform for emerging artists. Each month one recipient receives GBP 500, which can be spent on anything: making new work, equipment or materials, travel, research, visiting exhibitions or conferences, or covering living costs. No outcomes or reporting are expected. ELIGIBILITY: Black artists (those with Black heritage who identify as Black; not politically Black, POC or BAME) based in the UK, working in any creative discipline (painters, musicians, directors, jewellers, set designers, sculptors, choreographers and more), with no age limit. APPLY once via the BAG page; all applications stay on file and are reconsidered each month, and unsuccessful applicants are not notified. DEADLINE: rolling, monthly selection.

  234. Caza d'Oro Residency for Visual Artists (Le Mas d'Azil, France, rolling)

    Caza d'Oro, Centre International d'Art Contemporain · Le Mas d'Azil, Ariège, southwestern France. Housing (a furnished 50 m² apartment) and a 50 m² studio on site; families and pets cannot be accommodated. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: EUR 1,200 per month residency grant (EUR 3,600 over three months), plus a production budget of EUR 1,800 (Caza d'Oro's own site; the Arts en Résidence network lists EUR 2,000), housing, studio, outreach support and an end-of-residency exhibition. Travel costs are not mentioned.

    Caza d'Oro is an international contemporary art centre and residency in Le Mas d'Azil, Ariège, that invites artists to research and make work in the area, with public activities, outreach and an exhibition of the work made during the stay. It offers three three-month residencies for visual artists each year, selected by committee. TO APPLY: applications are accepted all year by email (cazadoro@cazadoro.org) or post, using the application form on the candidatures page. Artists selected for the following year are notified in July. No application fee is stated, and the published pages give no nationality, age or career-stage limits.

  235. Mondriaan Fund: Art Commission

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Commission artists to create new work in publicly accessible spaces such as hospitals or museums. Open to individuals and organisations. Continuous deadline.

  236. Mondriaan Fund: Artist Basic

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Support for visual artists with 4+ years of experience to expand their portfolio, increase visibility or conduct research. Continuous deadline.

  237. Mondriaan Fund: Artist Start

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Support for visual artists at the beginning of their careers with plans for new work. Continuous deadline.

  238. Mondriaan Fund: Curator Researcher

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Funding for preliminary research into exhibitions, events, articles or presentations. For curators. Continuous deadline.

  239. Mondriaan Fund: Protected Cultural Heritage

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Support for owners and managers of objects registered as protected heritage. Continuous deadline.

  240. Mondriaan Fund: Voucher Artisan

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Voucher to assist hiring artisans for artistic research or work production. Continuous deadline.

  241. Mondriaan Fund: Voucher Artist with Child

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Voucher covering childcare costs for visual artists with dependents under compulsory school age. Continuous deadline.

  242. Mondriaan Fund: Voucher Development

    Mondriaan Fund · Netherlands · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Funded (see grant page)

    Funding for developing and deepening artistic practice. Continuous deadline.

  243. VSBfonds: Kunst & Cultuur Donations (rolling, Netherlands)

    VSBfonds · European Netherlands. Private legal entities (foundations, associations); applicants without a registered legal form are also eligible. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: No fixed minimum or maximum; the requested amount must be in proportion to other funding sources. No application fee.

    VSBfonds supports cultural initiatives that make it possible for everyone in the Netherlands to take part in art and culture, spanning ten programme lines from professional performances to community arts. Applications are accepted year-round with no deadlines from foundations, associations and applicants without a formal legal form, and must be submitted at least four months before the initiative starts (two months for amateur arts). A two-minute online quickscan checks eligibility before the formal application. No fixed minimum or maximum amount; the request should be proportionate to other funding. No application fee.

  244. Canada Council for the Arts: Explore and Create, Artistic Creation (rolling)

    Canada Council for the Arts · Canada. For Canadian artists, groups and arts organizations. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Project grant; amounts are set in the program guidelines on the Council's portal. No application fee stated.

    Artistic Creation is the Canada Council's main creation grant within Explore and Create, and it now covers the activities previously funded by the Research and Creation and Concept to Realization components. It supports Canadian artists, groups and arts organizations in researching, developing and creating new work across disciplines, including digital arts and media arts practices such as interactive, net, generative, AI-driven and immersive work. INTAKE: continuous; apply any time before the start date of your project or activity (results usually take several months, so plan ahead). HOW TO APPLY: create a profile and apply through the Canada Council portal; detailed eligibility, grant amounts and project periods are in the guidelines there. Application Assistance is available for individuals who self-identify as Deaf or disabled, or as First Nations, Inuit or Metis. The related Artist-driven Organizations opportunity offers multi-year support to incorporated not-for-profit arts organizations.

  245. Canada Council for the Arts: Micro-grants (professional development and travel, rolling)

    Canada Council for the Arts · Canada. Canadian artists, arts workers, groups and organizations; travel within Canada or abroad. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Small grants; amounts set in the portal guidelines. No application fee.

    Micro-grants, under the Canada Council's Arts Across Canada and Abroad program, fund activities that advance the professional growth of artists, arts workers, groups and organizations, including travel to festivals, conferences, residencies, markets and professional development events in Canada or abroad. It replaces the former Explore and Create: Professional Development for Artists, Supporting Artistic Practice: Professional Development for Arts Professionals, Arts Across Canada: Travel and Arts Abroad: Travel components, and is open to all disciplines including digital and media arts. DEADLINE: rolling, any time before the start or departure date; notification usually within 4 months, so apply early. Related rolling streams: Representation and Promotion (travel to promote your work, before departure) and Creating, Knowing and Sharing: Travel for First Nations, Inuit and Metis artists (notification within 3 months). Application limits run on the calendar year. Apply through the Canada Council portal, where amounts and detailed eligibility are listed.

  246. Fonds Podiumkunsten: Urban Arts Projects 2027 (rolling from 1 January; up to EUR 15,000 for individuals, EUR 25,000 for collectives)

    Fonds Podiumkunsten (Performing Arts Fund NL) · Kingdom of the Netherlands (European and Caribbean). RESTRICTED: makers in urban culture without an art-school degree. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Up to EUR 15,000 for individuals and up to EUR 25,000 for companies and collectives, for time, materials and third-party services. No application fee mentioned.

    A project grant for theatre, dance, music and spoken-word makers rooted in urban culture who are established in their own scene but have not yet broken through nationally. The 2026 budget is spent; applications reopen on 1 January 2027 and are then handled continuously while the budget lasts. WHO: individuals, companies or collectives, aged 18 or over, with relevant stage experience performing their own material. Applicants must not be studying for, or hold, an art degree, and each maker can receive at most two grants through the programme. The project must work towards at least one live performance in the Kingdom. WHAT YOU GET: up to EUR 15,000 (individuals) or EUR 25,000 (collectives) for new work: your time, studio hire, performance materials and hired services. Equipment such as laptops or microphones is not covered. PROCESS: a short application is assessed within six weeks and followed by an interview; you then get four weeks to develop a full plan, with a decision six to eight weeks later. APPLICATION: through Mijn Fonds with an individual account: a form plus a PDF plan answering five questions (outcome, approach, audience, budget, existing audio or visual material). Contact: Soraya Ruijg, s.ruijg@fondspodiumkunsten.nl. DEADLINE: none; rolling from 1 January 2027 until the budget runs out, so early in the year is safest.

  247. Adobe Creative Residency Community Fund: USD 10,000 for visual creators affected by the invasion of Ukraine (rolling)

    Adobe (Adobe Creative Residency) · No fixed location; nothing to attend. RESTRICTED: creators directly affected by the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine (current residents of Ukraine, refugees or internally displaced people, or people financially supporting either). · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: USD 10,000 per selected creator, to be used at the recipient's full and lawful discretion; the stated purpose is to let recipients support themselves and their families. Paid to a PayPal or bank account in the applicant's own name. No application fee mentioned.

    A hardship fund run under Adobe's Creative Residency programme. The Community Fund responds to global events that affect the wellbeing of creators and concentrates on one issue for a sustained period; its current focus is creators directly affected by the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and Adobe says the focus may shift to a new issue later. WHO: creators with a professional portfolio of visual creative work who are at least 18 (no advanced degree needed), can communicate in English, hold a PayPal or bank account in their own name, and are one of the following: a refugee or internally displaced person because of the 2022 invasion, a current resident of Ukraine, or someone financially supporting either. Adobe is especially interested in video, photography, graphic design, illustration and product or interface design, but considers all types of work. WHAT YOU GET: USD 10,000 with no restriction on use. APPLICATION: through the Apply link on the fund page. No project proposal is needed; selection is based on the professional portfolio and on whether the applicant has been directly affected by the attacks on Ukraine. DEADLINE: none. Applications are accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis.

  248. Allianz Foundation Grants: Idea Portal (rolling; up to EUR 300,000 for socially engaged arts, trustworthy information and sustainable cities)

    Allianz Foundation · Europe: delivery and use of funds predominantly within the member states of the Council of Europe plus Kosovo (includes Turkey, Ukraine and the United Kingdom). Organisations only. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Generally up to EUR 300,000 per initiative, covering at most 75% of total costs; applicants must secure at least 25% from own or third-party funds (in-kind does not count). Up to 20% of costs may be claimed as administrative costs. No application fee stated.

    The Allianz Foundation funds projects and programmes across Europe that respond to linked ecological and social challenges. Its grants programme currently has three areas: Sustainable Cities, Trustworthy Information (production and distribution of public-interest information, viable models for public-interest media, collaborations between journalists, civil society and news creators) and Socially Engaged Arts (artistic initiatives that engage with ecological and social challenges and involve communities, with artistic freedom protected). WHO: non-profit organisations and other legal entities only; individuals cannot apply. Work must take place predominantly in Council of Europe member states plus Kosovo; transnational and cross-area projects are favoured. Excluded, among others: film productions (except project documentation), print products, media literacy projects, retrospectives, pure showcases, cultural education projects, individual scholarships and full financing. WHAT YOU GET: generally up to EUR 300,000 for 6 to 36 months, at most 75% of total costs, with up to 20% for administrative costs. APPLICATION: a short concept note in English through the Idea Portal form (about 15 minutes, cannot be saved); the foundation aims to reply within four weeks, then an informal conversation and, by invitation, a full application. DEADLINE: none stated; the portal accepts concept notes on a rolling basis.

  249. Guggenheim Museum: CHANEL Culture Fund Curatorial Fellowship (New York and Venice, one year from January 2027)

    Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, supported by CHANEL Culture Fund · New York, USA (1071 Fifth Avenue) for nine months, then the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice, Italy, for three months. The posting states no citizenship or visa terms. · Deadline: Rolling / undated · Award: Salary of USD 65,775.80 to USD 68,000 per year (full-time, exempt, covered by the collective bargaining agreement with Local 2110 UAW). No application fee mentioned.

    A one-year, salaried curatorial fellowship at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, made possible by CHANEL Culture Fund. It is a fixed-term, full-time staff position that offers practical museum training and exposure to how the multinational museum operates. The fellow spends nine months at Guggenheim New York working on curatorial initiatives around the museum's history, collections and scholarship, then three months at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice on project-based research. WHO: holders of a Master's degree, or PhD candidates, in art history, with a background in early and/or mid 20th century art, fluency in English and Italian, and proficiency with collection management databases such as The Museum System (TMS); previous museum curatorial experience is preferred. WHAT YOU DO: scholarly and provenance research on collection works, exhibition and publication histories, object-based and conservation-related research with the Conservation Department, gallery texts and labels, research content for the website, and guided tours. In New York the fellow supports the installation of the exhibition Peggy Guggenheim in London: The Making of a Collector; in Venice, the reinstallation of the collection, with the option of joining the educational activities of the Peggy Guggenheim Collection's International Fellowship Program. WHAT YOU GET: an annual salary of USD 65,775.80 to USD 68,000. APPLICATION: through the Guggenheim's applicant portal at the link. DEADLINE: none is stated in the posting; the position starts in January 2027, so apply promptly.
